decks.title: Linear Inequations — Part 1: Replacement sets and solving
goals: Find the solution set of a linear inequation for a given replacement set
Solve linear inequations using the rules for inequalities
Explain why the sign reverses when multiplying or dividing by a negative number
Write solution sets in roster and set-builder form

slides.heading: Linear Inequations, Part 1
slides.body_md: An equation has one answer; an inequation usually has many. Which ones count depends on the replacement set.

slides.narration: Welcome to linear inequations. An equation such as three x plus two equals fourteen has one answer. An inequation such as three x plus two is less than fourteen has many answers. In this part you will find all of them, for different sets of numbers, and learn the one rule that makes inequations different from equations.

slides.heading: What you will be able to do
bullets: Solve a linear inequation step by step
Reverse the sign when multiplying or dividing by a **negative** number
Write the answer in roster or set-builder form
slides.narration: These are your goals for part one. First the signs and the replacement sets. Then the rules for solving, which are almost the same as for equations, with one important exception. Finally, how to write the solution set neatly, the way the board expects.

slides.heading: Inequality signs
slides.body_md: A **linear inequation** in one variable compares two expressions such as $3x + 2$ and $14$ with one of four signs.

rows: is less than or equal to
is greater than or equal to

visual.alt: Table of the four inequality signs: less than, less than or equal to, greater than, greater than or equal to. With the examples x less than 3 and x greater than 3, the number 3 is not a solution; with less than or equal to and greater than or equal to, it is.
visual.caption: The sign decides whether the boundary number belongs.

slides.narration: There are four signs. Less than, and greater than, are strict: the boundary number does not count. Less than or equal to, and greater than or equal to, include the boundary. Look at the last column: three is a solution of x is less than or equal to three, but not of x is less than three.

slides.heading: Replacement set and solution set
slides.body_md: The **replacement set** is the set of numbers $x$ may take. The **solution set** is the set of those numbers that make the inequation true.

rows: all numbers on the number line, including fractions and decimals

visual.alt: Table of replacement sets: natural numbers N start at 1; whole numbers W start at 0; integers Z include the negative whole numbers; real numbers R include every point of the number line.
visual.caption: The four replacement sets used in this chapter.

slides.narration: Every inequation comes with a replacement set: the numbers you are allowed to try. Natural numbers start at one. Whole numbers start at zero. Integers include the negatives. Real numbers fill the whole number line. The solution set is the part of the replacement set that makes the statement true.

slides.heading: One inequation, four replacement sets
slides.body_md: $3x - 2 \le 7$ simplifies to $x \le 3$. The solution set depends on where $x$ comes from:

visual.alt: Table for 3x minus 2 at most 7, which simplifies to x at most 3: over N the solution set is 1, 2, 3; over W it is 0, 1, 2, 3; over Z it is 3, 2, 1 and every smaller integer; over R it is every real number up to and including 3.
visual.caption: One inequation, four different solution sets.

slides.narration: Here is the same inequation in four replacement sets. It simplifies to x is at most three. For natural numbers, the answer is one, two and three. Whole numbers add zero. Integers go on for ever to the left. For real numbers we cannot list the answer, so we describe it in set builder form.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: testing members
slides.body_md: Find the solution set of $3x + 2 < 14$ for (a) $x \in \mathbb{W}$ (b) $x \in \mathbb{N}$.

visual.alt: Table testing whole numbers in 3x plus 2 less than 14: for x equal to 0, 1, 2 and 3 the value is 2, 5, 8 and 11, all less than 14; for 4 and 5 it is 14 and 17, which are not.
visual.caption: Testing members agrees with solving: $x < 4$.

slides.narration: Subtract two from both sides: three x is less than twelve. Divide by three: x is less than four. The table confirms it: zero, one, two and three give values below fourteen, but four gives exactly fourteen, which is not less than fourteen. For natural numbers, drop the zero.

slides.heading: Quick check: natural numbers
slides.body_md: Solve, then keep only natural numbers.
slides.narration: Subtract four from both sides first. Then list the natural numbers that are smaller, and remember that zero is not a natural number.

slides.heading: Rules for solving an inequation
slides.body_md: Like an equation, an inequation stays true when you add, subtract, multiply or divide both sides by the same number, **except** that multiplying or dividing by a **negative** number reverses the sign.

headers: Do this to both sides of $2 < 7$

visual.alt: Table of operations on 2 less than 7: adding 5 gives 7 less than 12, subtracting 3 gives minus 1 less than 4, multiplying by 4 gives 8 less than 28, dividing by 2 gives 1 less than 3.5; multiplying by minus 3 gives minus 6 greater than minus 21, and dividing by minus 1 gives minus 2 greater than minus 7.
visual.caption: Only a negative multiplier or divisor reverses the sign.

slides.narration: The rules are nearly the same as for equations. Adding or subtracting the same number keeps the sign. Multiplying or dividing by a positive number keeps the sign. But multiply or divide by a negative number, and the sign must be turned round. Two is less than seven, but minus six is greater than minus twenty one.

slides.heading: Why the sign reverses
slides.body_md: Multiplying by $-1$ reflects every number in $0$. A number that was to the left moves to the right.

slides.narration: Why does a negative number reverse the sign? Multiplying by minus one reflects the number line in zero. Two is to the left of five, so two is less than five. Their mirror images are minus two and minus five, and now minus two is to the right. So minus two is greater than minus five.

slides.heading: Writing the solution set
slides.body_md: Use **roster form** when the members can be listed, and **set-builder form** for real numbers.

rows: a list that goes on for ever
real numbers, which cannot be listed

visual.alt: Table of ways to write a solution set: roster form lists the members, possibly with dots for a list that goes on; set-builder form describes real-number solutions; the empty set is written phi.
visual.caption: Choose the form that fits the replacement set.

slides.narration: Use roster form when you can list the members, with three dots if the list goes on. Use set builder form for real numbers, because between any two real numbers there are infinitely many more. If nothing satisfies the inequation, the solution set is the empty set, written phi.

Read a solution set from a graph
slides.narration: These are your goals for part two. Combined inequations first, then pairs of inequations and their common solutions. Throughout, we represent answers on the number line, and we learn to read a graph back into set notation.

slides.heading: Combined (double) inequations
slides.body_md: $-3 \le 2x + 1 < 9$ means $-3 \le 2x + 1$ **and** $2x + 1 < 9$. Work on all three parts at once:

nodes.label: Do the same step to **all three** parts
Dividing by a negative number: reverse **both** signs
Rewrite with the smaller number on the left
Pick members of the replacement set

visual.alt: Flow chart for a combined inequation: do the same step to all three parts; when dividing by a negative number reverse both signs; rewrite with the smaller number on the left; then pick the members of the replacement set.
visual.caption: Solving a combined (double) inequation.

slides.narration: A combined inequation is two inequations written as one. Minus three is at most two x plus one, and two x plus one is less than nine. We can solve both together by doing the same step to all three parts. If we divide by a negative number, both signs reverse, and we then rewrite the answer with the smaller number first.

slides.heading: Filled and open circles
slides.body_md: On the number line for $\mathbb{R}$: **filled circle** = end point included ($\le$, $\ge$); **open circle** = end point excluded ($<$, $>$).

slides.heading: Worked example 4: a word problem
slides.body_md: An imagined goods lift carries at most $680$ kg. Its operator weighs $72$ kg and each box weighs $38$ kg. How many boxes can go up with the operator?
bullets: **Step 1 —** Let $x$ be the number of boxes: $72 + 38x \le 680$.
**Answer —** at most $16$ boxes ($x$ is a whole number).

visual.alt: Table of lift loads: 14 boxes give 604 kilograms, 15 give 642, 16 give exactly 680, which is allowed, and 17 give 718, which is too much.
visual.caption: The boundary value $16$ is allowed because the sign is $\le$.

slides.narration: Let x be the number of boxes. The load is seventy two plus thirty eight x, and it must be at most six hundred and eighty. Subtract seventy two and divide by thirty eight: x is at most sixteen. Sixteen boxes give exactly six hundred and eighty kilograms, which is allowed. Seventeen would be too heavy.

slides.body_md: Find the real numbers that satisfy both $2x - 1 > 7$ and $3x + 2 < 8$.
bullets: **Answer —** no number is greater than $4$ and less than $2$, so the solution set is $\phi$.

sections.heading: 1. Linear inequations and the four signs
sections.body_md:
A **linear inequation** in one variable compares two linear expressions with one of the signs $<$, $\le$, $>$, $\ge$, for example $3x + 2 < 14$.

- $<$ and $>$ are **strict**: the boundary number is not a solution.
- $\le$ and $\ge$ include the boundary: $x = 3$ satisfies $x \le 3$ but not $x < 3$.

key_terms.definition_md: A statement such as $ax + b < c$ (or with $\le$, $>$, $\ge$) in which the variable has power $1$.
One with $<$ or $>$; the boundary value is excluded.

rows: is less than or equal to
is greater than or equal to

visual.alt: Table of the four inequality signs: less than, less than or equal to, greater than, greater than or equal to. With the examples x less than 3 and x greater than 3, the number 3 is not a solution; with less than or equal to and greater than or equal to, it is.
visual.caption: The sign decides whether the boundary number belongs.

sections.heading: 2. Replacement set and solution set
sections.body_md:
The **replacement set** (domain) is the set from which $x$ is taken: $\mathbb{N} = \{1, 2, 3, \ldots\}$, $\mathbb{W} = \{0, 1, 2, \ldots\}$, $\mathbb{Z} = \{\ldots, -1, 0, 1, \ldots\}$ or $\mathbb{R}$, or a set given in the question. The **solution set** is the subset whose members make the inequation true.

*Example:* $3x - 2 \le 7$ gives $x \le 3$: over $\mathbb{N}$, $\{1, 2, 3\}$; over $\mathbb{W}$, $\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$; over $\mathbb{Z}$, $\{\ldots, 1, 2, 3\}$.

key_terms.definition_md: The set of values the variable may take.
The members of the replacement set that satisfy the inequation.
A solution set with no members, written $\phi$ or $\{\ \}$.

rows: all numbers on the number line, including fractions and decimals

sections.heading: 3. Rules for solving
sections.body_md:
An inequation keeps its solution set when you

- add or subtract the same number (or expression) on both sides;
- multiply or divide both sides by the same **positive** number.

Then solve as for an equation: remove brackets, clear fractions with the LCM (multiply **every** term), collect $x$ terms on one side and numbers on the other.

*Example:* $\dfrac{x}{3} - 1 \le \dfrac{x - 2}{4}$; multiply by $12$: $4x - 12 \le 3x - 6$, so $x \le 6$.

sections.heading: 4. Multiplying or dividing by a negative number
sections.body_md:
Multiplying or dividing both sides by a **negative** number **reverses** the sign: $<$ becomes $>$ and $\le$ becomes $\ge$.

**Why:** multiplying by $-1$ reflects the number line in $0$, so the order of any two numbers is turned round: $2 < 5$ but $-2 > -5$.

*Example:* $7 - 3x \ge -8 \Rightarrow -3x \ge -15 \Rightarrow x \le 5$ (dividing by $-3$).

sections.heading: 5. Combined (double) inequations
sections.body_md:
$a < px + q \le b$ means $a < px + q$ **and** $px + q \le b$.

- When $x$ appears only in the middle, do the same step to all three parts; dividing by a negative number reverses **both** signs. Rewrite with the smaller number on the left.
- When $x$ appears in all three parts (e.g. $3x - 7 < 2x + 1 \le 4x + 6$), split it into two inequations and take the common part.

*Example:* $5 < 11 - 2x \le 17 \Rightarrow -6 < -2x \le 6 \Rightarrow 3 > x \ge -3$, i.e. $-3 \le x < 3$.

key_terms.definition_md: Two inequations written together, such as $-3 \le 2x + 1 < 9$.

sections.heading: 7. Two inequations: intersection, union and the empty set
sections.body_md:
For $A = \{x : \ldots\}$ and $B = \{x : \ldots\}$, solve each separately.

- $A \cap B$: numbers in both, the overlap of the two graphs. *Example:* $x > -2$ and $x \le 4$ give $-2 < x \le 4$.
- $A \cup B$: numbers in at least one of them.
- If the graphs do not overlap ($x > 4$ and $x < 2$), $A \cap B = \phi$.

key_terms.definition_md: The set of numbers satisfying both inequations, $A \cap B$.
The set of numbers satisfying at least one inequation, $A \cup B$.

notes.exam_tips_md:
**How marks are awarded**
- *Solve and write the solution set (2–3 marks):* correct steps 1–2; solution set in the right form 1.
- *Combined inequation (3–4 marks):* same step on all parts 1; reversal of both signs 1; solution set 1; number line 1.
- *Number line (1 mark):* dots for $\mathbb{N}$, $\mathbb{W}$, $\mathbb{Z}$; thick line for $\mathbb{R}$; filled or open circles; arrows.
- *10-mark structured question:* parts (a), (b), (c) usually 3 + 3 + 4; show all working.

**Common mistakes**
1. Not reversing the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number (or reversing only one sign of a combined inequation).
2. Including $0$ in $\mathbb{N}$, or negative numbers in $\mathbb{W}$.
3. Forgetting to multiply a whole-number term when clearing fractions.
4. Filled circle for $<$ or $>$; open circle for $\le$ or $\ge$.
5. Joining dots with a line for integers, or listing a real-number solution set.
6. Leaving out the arrow when the solution set goes on for ever.

cards.front_md: What is a **linear inequation** in one variable?
cards.back_md: A statement comparing two linear expressions in $x$ with $<$, $\le$, $>$ or $\ge$, e.g. $3x + 2 < 14$.

cards.front_md: What is a **replacement set**?
cards.back_md: The set of values the variable is allowed to take.

cards.front_md: What is a **solution set**?
cards.back_md: The members of the replacement set that make the inequation true.

cards.front_md: List the start of $\mathbb{N}$ and of $\mathbb{W}$.
cards.back_md: $\mathbb{N} = \{1, 2, 3, \ldots\}$; $\mathbb{W} = \{0, 1, 2, \ldots\}$

cards.front_md: What does $\mathbb{Z}$ contain that $\mathbb{W}$ does not?
cards.back_md: The negative integers $-1, -2, -3, \ldots$

cards.front_md: Is $3$ a solution of $x < 3$? Of $x \le 3$?
cards.back_md: No; yes.

cards.front_md: $3x - 2 \le 7$ over $\mathbb{N}$, $\mathbb{W}$?
How is the empty set written?
Which operations keep the inequality sign?
cards.back_md: Adding or subtracting any number; multiplying or dividing by a positive number.

cards.front_md: When is the inequality sign reversed?
cards.back_md: When both sides are multiplied or divided by a negative number.

cards.front_md: Why does multiplying by $-1$ reverse the sign?
cards.back_md: It reflects the number line in $0$, turning the order round: $2 < 5$ but $-2 > -5$.

cards.front_md: Solve $-3x \ge -15$.
cards.back_md: $x \le 5$ (divide by $-3$, reverse the sign).

cards.front_md: Clearing fractions in $\dfrac{x}{3} - 1 \le \dfrac{x - 2}{4}$: multiply by?
cards.back_md: $12$, every term, including the $1$.

cards.front_md: What does $-3 \le 2x + 1 < 9$ mean?
Combined inequation: how do you solve it?
cards.back_md: Do the same step to all three parts.

cards.front_md: Dividing all parts of $-6 < -2x \le 6$ by $-2$ gives?
$x$ appears in all three parts, e.g. $3x - 7 < 2x + 1 \le 4x + 6$. Method?
cards.back_md: Split into two inequations, solve each, take the common part.

cards.front_md: Roster or set-builder form for $x \in \mathbb{R}$?
cards.back_md: Set-builder form, e.g. $\{x : x \in \mathbb{R},\ x > 4.5\}$.

cards.front_md: What does $A \cap B$ mean for two inequations?
cards.back_md: The numbers that satisfy both: the overlap of their graphs.

cards.front_md: $x > 4$ and $x < 2$: common solution?
cards.back_md: None: $\phi$.

cards.front_md: Filled circle on a number line means…
cards.back_md: the end point is included ($\le$ or $\ge$).

cards.front_md: Open circle on a number line means…
cards.back_md: the end point is excluded ($<$ or $>$).

cards.front_md: Graph of a solution set in $\mathbb{Z}$?
cards.back_md: Separate filled dots, not a line.

cards.front_md: Graph of $x > 4.5$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$?
cards.back_md: Open circle at $4.5$, thick line with an arrow to the right.

cards.front_md: Graph: filled circle at $-1$, open circle at $4$, thick line. Set?
cards.back_md: $\{x : x \in \mathbb{R},\ -1 \le x < 4\}$

cards.front_md: When does a number-line graph need an arrow?
cards.back_md: When the solution set goes on for ever in that direction.

cards.front_md: Most common sign mistake?
cards.back_md: Forgetting to reverse the sign when dividing by a negative number.

cards.front_md: Greatest integer with $x < 7.5$?
Word problem: "at most" and "at least" become?
cards.back_md: "At most" is $\le$; "at least" is $\ge$.

cards.front_md: How do you check a solution set?
cards.back_md: Substitute a member (it must work) and a number just outside (it must fail).

questions.stem_md: In this chapter $\mathbb{W}$ names the replacement set of whole numbers. Which set is $\mathbb{W}$?

options.text_md: every real number, including fractions and decimals

questions.solution_md: $\mathbb{W}$ is the natural numbers together with $0$. Option (b) is $\mathbb{N}$, (c) is $\mathbb{Z}$ and (d) is $\mathbb{R}$.

questions.stem_md: With the replacement set $\mathbb{N}$, the solution set of $x + 4 < 9$ is
questions.solution_md: $x + 4 < 9 \Rightarrow x < 5$. The natural numbers less than $5$ are $1, 2, 3, 4$. Option (c) includes $0$, which is not a natural number; (d) includes $5$, but $5 < 5$ is false.

questions.stem_md: For $x \in \mathbb{W}$, which is the solution set of $2x - 3 \le 4$?
questions.solution_md: $2x - 3 \le 4 \Rightarrow 2x \le 7 \Rightarrow x \le 3.5$. The whole numbers up to $3.5$ are $0, 1, 2, 3$. Option (d) leaves out $0$; (a) rounds $3.5$ up to $4$, which does not satisfy the inequation.

questions.stem_md: Both sides of $-4x > 12$ are divided by $-4$. The result is
questions.solution_md: Dividing by a negative number reverses the sign: $-4x > 12 \Rightarrow x < -3$. Check with $x = -4$: $16 > 12$ is true. Option (a) forgets to reverse the sign.

questions.stem_md: Find the solution set of $5 - 2x > 11$ when the replacement set is $\mathbb{Z}$.
questions.solution_md: $5 - 2x > 11 \Rightarrow -2x > 6 \Rightarrow x < -3$, so the integers are $-4, -5, -6$ and every smaller integer. Option (b) does not reverse the sign; (c) wrongly includes $-3$.

questions.stem_md: What is the greatest integer $x$ for which $3(x - 2) < x + 9$?
questions.solution_md: $3x - 6 < x + 9 \Rightarrow 2x < 15 \Rightarrow x < 7.5$. The greatest integer less than $7.5$ is $7$. Option (d) is not an integer, and (c) is too large: $3 \times 6 = 18$ is not less than $17$.

questions.stem_md: For $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the solution set of $\dfrac{x}{2} + 3 \ge \dfrac{x}{3} + 4$ is
questions.solution_md: Multiply both sides by $6$: $3x + 18 \ge 2x + 24 \Rightarrow x \ge 6$. Option (b) comes from $\dfrac{x}{6} \ge 1$ without multiplying the $1$ by $6$.

questions.stem_md: Which picture on the number line shows the solution set of $x < 2$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$?

options.text_md: a filled circle at 2, with a thick line and an arrow going to the left
an open circle at 2, with a thick line and an arrow going to the right
separate filled dots at 1, 0, −1, −2 and so on
an open circle at 2, with a thick line and an arrow going to the left

questions.solution_md: $2$ itself is not included, so its circle is open; every real number less than $2$ is included, so the line is thick all the way to the left. Dots, as in (c), are used only for $\mathbb{N}$, $\mathbb{W}$ or $\mathbb{Z}$.

questions.stem_md: If $x \in \mathbb{Z}$, the solution set of the combined inequation $-5 < 3x + 1 \le 10$ is
questions.solution_md: Subtract $1$ from all three parts and divide by $3$: $-6 < 3x \le 9 \Rightarrow -2 < x \le 3$. $-2$ is excluded (strict sign) and $3$ is included.

questions.stem_md: Which is the solution set of $-2 \le 1 - x < 3$ for whole-number values of $x$?
questions.solution_md: $-3 \le -x < 2$; multiplying by $-1$ reverses both signs: $3 \ge x > -2$. The whole numbers in this range are $0, 1, 2, 3$. Option (c) includes $-1$, which is not a whole number.

questions.stem_md: The number line below shows the solution set of a combined inequation in $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Read it and choose the set it shows.
questions.solution_md: The filled circle at $-1$ means $-1$ is included ($\le$); the open circle at $4$ means $4$ is excluded ($<$). Option (d) swaps the two kinds of circle.

questions.stem_md: On a number line for $x \in \mathbb{R}$, a solution set is drawn as a filled circle at $3$ with a thick line and an arrow to the left. Which inequation has this solution set?
questions.solution_md: $2x - 1 \le 5 \Rightarrow 2x \le 6 \Rightarrow x \le 3$: every real number up to and including $3$. Option (a) gives $x < 3$ (open circle), (b) gives $x \ge 3$ (arrow to the right) and (c) gives $x \le 2$.

questions.stem_md: $A = \{x : x \in \mathbb{R},\ 2x + 1 > -5\}$ and $B = \{x : x \in \mathbb{R},\ 3x - 4 \le 8\}$. Then $A \cap B$ is
questions.solution_md: $2x + 1 > -5 \Rightarrow x > -3$ and $3x - 4 \le 8 \Rightarrow x \le 4$. The numbers in both sets satisfy $-3 < x \le 4$. Option (b) swaps the strict and non-strict ends.

questions.stem_md: How many natural numbers belong to the solution set of $4x - 7 < 2x + 9$?
questions.solution_md: $4x - 7 < 2x + 9 \Rightarrow 2x < 16 \Rightarrow x < 8$, so the solution set is $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\}$: seven numbers. Option (c) also counts $8$, or counts $0$.

questions.stem_md: Rhea solved $6 - 3x \le 18$ for $x \in \mathbb{R}$ like this: "$-3x \le 12$, so $x \le -4$." What is the correct solution?
questions.solution_md: Her division by $-3$ did not reverse the sign. Correctly, $6 - 3x \le 18 \Rightarrow -3x \le 12 \Rightarrow x \ge -4$. Check with $x = 0$: $6 \le 18$ is true, and $0 \ge -4$.

questions.stem_md: For which replacement set is the solution set of $x - 3 < -1$ exactly $\{0, 1\}$?
questions.solution_md: $x - 3 < -1 \Rightarrow x < 2$. Over $\mathbb{W}$ this is $\{0, 1\}$; over $\mathbb{N}$ only $\{1\}$; over $\mathbb{Z}$ it also contains $-1, -2, \ldots$; over $\mathbb{R}$ it contains every real number less than $2$.

questions.stem_md: Find the smallest integer that satisfies $2 - 5x < 3x - 22$.
questions.solution_md: $2 - 5x < 3x - 22 \Rightarrow -8x < -24 \Rightarrow x > 3$. $3$ itself is excluded, so the smallest integer is $4$. Option (c) comes from a sign slip with $-24$.

questions.stem_md: When a solution set over the real numbers is drawn on a number line, what does an open (hollow) circle at an end point tell you?

options.text_md: the solution set contains only that end point
that end point is not a member of the solution set
that end point is a member of the solution set

questions.solution_md: An open circle marks an excluded end point (from < or >); a filled circle marks an included one (from ≤ or ≥).

questions.stem_md: Solve the combined inequation $-7 \le 2 - 3x < 8$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$.
questions.solution_md: Subtract $2$: $-9 \le -3x < 6$. Divide by $-3$ and reverse both signs: $3 \ge x > -2$, that is $-2 < x \le 3$. Option (d) forgets that the strict and non-strict signs swap ends.

questions.stem_md: Let $x \in \mathbb{Z}$, $P = \{x : 1 - x \ge -3\}$ and $Q = \{x : 2x + 3 > -3\}$. Which set is $P \cap Q$?
questions.solution_md: $1 - x \ge -3 \Rightarrow -x \ge -4 \Rightarrow x \le 4$; $2x + 3 > -3 \Rightarrow 2x > -6 \Rightarrow x > -3$. The integers with $-3 < x \le 4$ are $-2$ to $4$. Option (a) wrongly includes $-3$.

questions.solution_md: $2x < 2 \Rightarrow x < 1$, and no natural number is less than $1$, so the solution set is $\phi$.

questions.stem_md: The solution set of $3 - x > 1$, $x \in \mathbb{W}$, is $\{0, 1, 2\}$.
questions.solution_md: $-x > -2 \Rightarrow x < 2$, so the set is $\{0, 1\}$; $2$ is excluded because $3 - 2 = 1$ is not greater than $1$.

questions.stem_md: Every member of the solution set of $x \le 4$, $x \in \mathbb{N}$, is also a member of the solution set of $x \le 4$, $x \in \mathbb{Z}$.
questions.solution_md: $\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ is part of $\{\ldots, 2, 3, 4\}$, because every natural number is an integer.

questions.stem_md: Over $\mathbb{R}$, the inequations $5x - 2 \ge 3x + 6$ and $x \ge 4$ have the same solution set.
questions.solution_md: $5x - 2 \ge 3x + 6 \Rightarrow 2x \ge 8 \Rightarrow x \ge 4$; each step keeps the solution set.

questions.stem_md: The solution set of $1 < x < 3$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$, is $\{2\}$.
questions.solution_md: $\{2\}$ is the answer for $x \in \mathbb{Z}$. Over $\mathbb{R}$, every real number between $1$ and $3$ belongs, such as $1.5$ and $2.9$.

questions.stem_md: If $x \in \mathbb{W}$ and $4x < 13$, the greatest member of the solution set is ___.
questions.solution_md: $4x < 13 \Rightarrow x < 3.25$; the greatest whole number below $3.25$ is $3$.

questions.stem_md: For $x \in \mathbb{Z}$, the solution set of $-3 < x \le 1$ has ___ members.
questions.solution_md: The set is $\{-2, -1, 0, 1\}$, so it has $4$ members ($-3$ is excluded, $1$ is included).

questions.stem_md: Dividing both sides of $-5x \ge 20$ by $-5$ gives $x$ ___ $-4$ (write the sign).
questions.solution_md: Dividing by a negative number reverses the sign, so x is less than or equal to $-4$: $x \le -4$.

questions.stem_md: The smallest integer satisfying $7x + 3 > 2x - 12$ is ___.
questions.solution_md: $7x + 3 > 2x - 12 \Rightarrow 5x > -15 \Rightarrow x > -3$, so the smallest integer is $-2$.

questions.stem_md: On a number line, an end point that does not belong to the solution set is marked with an ___ circle.
questions.solution_md: An open (hollow) circle shows the end point is excluded; a filled circle shows it is included.

questions.stem_md: Over $\mathbb{R}$, the inequation $\dfrac{x}{2} - 1 \le 1$ simplifies to $x \le$ ___.
questions.solution_md: $\dfrac{x}{2} - 1 \le 1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{x}{2} \le 2 \Rightarrow x \le 4$.

questions.stem_md: A taxi in an imagined hill town charges ₹50 to start and ₹15 per kilometre. With ₹200, the greatest whole number of kilometres Neha can travel is ___.
questions.solution_md: $50 + 15x \le 200 \Rightarrow 15x \le 150 \Rightarrow x \le 10$, so she can travel at most $10$ km.

questions.stem_md: How many whole numbers satisfy $3x - 4 < 11$?
questions.solution_md: $3x - 4 < 11 \Rightarrow 3x < 15 \Rightarrow x < 5$, so $x \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}$: $5$ whole numbers.

questions.stem_md: Find the sum of all the integers $x$ for which $-4 \le 2x + 2 < 7$.
questions.solution_md: $-6 \le 2x < 5 \Rightarrow -3 \le x < 2.5$. The integers are $-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2$, and their sum is $-3$.

questions.stem_md: Find the largest integer $x$ that satisfies $\dfrac{2x - 1}{3} \le \dfrac{x + 4}{2}$.
questions.solution_md: Multiply by $6$: $2(2x - 1) \le 3(x + 4)$, so $4x - 2 \le 3x + 12 \Rightarrow x \le 14$. The largest integer is $14$.

questions.stem_md: Find the smallest natural number $x$ for which $5x - 11 > 2(x + 8)$.
questions.solution_md: $5x - 11 > 2x + 16 \Rightarrow 3x > 27 \Rightarrow x > 9$. $9$ is excluded, so the smallest natural number is $10$.

questions.stem_md: An imagined mobile plan costs ₹99 a month plus ₹1.50 for every minute of calls. Farida wants her bill to be at most ₹300. Find the greatest whole number of minutes she can use.
questions.solution_md: $99 + 1.5x \le 300 \Rightarrow 1.5x \le 201 \Rightarrow x \le 134$. She can use at most $134$ minutes.

answer.model_answer_md:
Multiply both sides by $12$:

$3x + 9 - 4x + 4 < 12$

$-x + 13 < 12 \Rightarrow -x < -1 \Rightarrow x > 1$

Solution set $= \{x : x \in \mathbb{R},\ x > 1\}$.

$4 \ge x > -6$

So $-6 < x \le 4$ and the solution set is $\{-5, -4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}$.

questions.stem_md: An imagined garden bed is a rectangle with length $(2x + 3)$ m and breadth $x$ m. Its perimeter must be at most 54 m, and its breadth at least 4 m. Find all the whole-number values of $x$ that are possible.

answer.model_answer_md:
Perimeter condition:

$2(2x + 3 + x) \le 54$

$6x + 6 \le 54 \Rightarrow 6x \le 48 \Rightarrow x \le 8$

Breadth condition: $x \ge 4$.

So $4 \le x \le 8$, and the possible values are $\{4, 5, 6, 7, 8\}$.

questions.stem_md: Kiran solved $4 - 3x \ge 10$, $x \in \mathbb{Z}$, as: "$-3x \ge 6$, so $x \ge -2$, and the solution set is $\{-2, -1, 0, \ldots\}$." Find his mistake and write the correct solution set. Test one member of each set.

answer.model_answer_md:
Kiran divided by $-3$ without reversing the sign.

Correct: $4 - 3x \ge 10 \Rightarrow -3x \ge 6 \Rightarrow x \le -2$, so the solution set is $\{\ldots, -4, -3, -2\}$.

Test: $x = -2$ gives $4 + 6 = 10 \ge 10$, true. Kiran's member $x = 0$ gives $4 \ge 10$, false.

questions.stem_md: Solve $3x - 7 < 2x + 1 \le 4x + 6$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$, and describe the graph of the solution set on the number line.

answer.model_answer_md:
Split into two inequations.

(i) $3x - 7 < 2x + 1 \Rightarrow x < 8$.

(ii) $2x + 1 \le 4x + 6 \Rightarrow -2x \le 5 \Rightarrow x \ge -\dfrac{5}{2}$.

Both hold when $-\dfrac{5}{2} \le x < 8$, i.e. $\{x : x \in \mathbb{R},\ -2.5 \le x < 8\}$.

Number line: a filled circle at $-2.5$, an open circle at $8$, and a thick line joining them.

questions.stem_md: Solve $-1 \le 2 - \dfrac{x + 1}{2} < 3$, $x \in \mathbb{Z}$, and represent the solution set on the number line.

answer.model_answer_md:
Multiply by $2$:

$-2 \le 4 - (x + 1) < 6$

Simplify:

$-2 \le 3 - x < 6$

Subtract $3$:

$-5 \le -x < 3$

Multiply by $-1$ and reverse both signs:

$5 \ge x > -3$

So $-3 < x \le 5$; solution set $= \{-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$.

Number line: filled dots at $-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4$ and $5$ only.

questions.stem_md: $A = \{x : x \in \mathbb{R},\ 5 - 2x \le 11\}$ and $B = \{x : x \in \mathbb{R},\ 4x - 3 < 13\}$. Find $A \cap B$ and describe it on the number line.

answer.model_answer_md:

$B$: $4x - 3 < 13 \Rightarrow 4x < 16 \Rightarrow x < 4$.

$A \cap B$: $-3 \le x < 4$, i.e. $\{x : x \in \mathbb{R},\ -3 \le x < 4\}$.

questions.stem_md: Three times a natural number, decreased by 4, is greater than 11. Twice the same number, increased by 5, is at most 27. Form two inequations and find every possible value of the number.

answer.model_answer_md:
Let the number be $x \in \mathbb{N}$.

$3x - 4 > 11 \Rightarrow 3x > 15 \Rightarrow x > 5$.

$2x + 5 \le 27 \Rightarrow 2x \le 22 \Rightarrow x \le 11$.

So $5 < x \le 11$, and the number is one of $\{6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11\}$.

questions.stem_md: Solve $\dfrac{x - 1}{4} + 1 > \dfrac{x + 3}{6}$, $x \in \mathbb{Z}$. Write the solution set, state its smallest member and describe its graph.

answer.model_answer_md:
Multiply by $12$:

$3(x - 1) + 12 > 2(x + 3)$

$3x + 9 > 2x + 6 \Rightarrow x > -3$

Solution set $= \{-2, -1, 0, \ldots\}$; the smallest member is $-2$.

Number line: filled dots at $-2, -1, 0, 1, \ldots$ continuing to the right; no dot at $-3$.

questions.stem_md: The replacement set is $\{-5, -4, -3, \ldots, 4, 5\}$. Find the values of $x$ in it that satisfy both $2x + 1 > x - 2$ and $3x - 2 \le 5$.

$3x - 2 \le 5 \Rightarrow 3x \le 7 \Rightarrow x \le \dfrac{7}{3}$, i.e. $x \le 2\tfrac{1}{3}$: $\{-5, -4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2\}$.

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) $7 - 2x > 3x - 8 \Rightarrow -5x > -15 \Rightarrow x < 3$. Solution set $= \{1, 2\}$.

(b) Multiply by $6$: $2(x + 2) \ge 3(x - 1)$, so $2x + 4 \ge 3x - 3 \Rightarrow -x \ge -7 \Rightarrow x \le 7$.

Solution set $= \{x : x \in \mathbb{R},\ x \le 7\}$: a filled circle at $7$ and a thick line with an arrow to the left.

(c) Multiply by $5$: $-10 \le 2x - 3 < 5$. Add $3$ and divide by $2$: $-7 \le 2x < 8 \Rightarrow -3.5 \le x < 4$.

Solution set $= \{x : x \in \mathbb{R},\ -3.5 \le x < 4\}$: a filled circle at $-3.5$, an open circle at $4$ and a thick line joining them.

questions.stem_md:
Form an inequation for each situation and solve it.

(a) An imagined coach company charges ₹1,200 to hire a bus for a school trip plus ₹35 for each student. The class has ₹3,000. Find the greatest number of students who can go.

(b) The sum of two consecutive odd natural numbers is greater than 30 but less than 50. Find all such pairs.

(c) Priya scored 62, 71 and 58 marks (out of 100) in three tests. She wants an average of at least 65 over four tests. Find the least whole-number score she needs in the fourth test, and the set of possible scores.

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Let $x$ students go: $1200 + 35x \le 3000 \Rightarrow 35x \le 1800 \Rightarrow x \le \dfrac{360}{7}$. Since $\dfrac{360}{7} \approx 51.4$ and $x$ is a whole number, at most $51$ students can go.

(b) Let the smaller number be $x$; the next odd number is $x + 2$. $30 < 2x + 2 < 50$, so $28 < 2x < 48 \Rightarrow 14 < x < 24$.

The odd numbers between $14$ and $24$ are $15, 17, 19, 21, 23$, giving the pairs $(15, 17)$, $(17, 19)$, $(19, 21)$, $(21, 23)$ and $(23, 25)$.

(c) Let her fourth score be $x$: $\dfrac{62 + 71 + 58 + x}{4} \ge 65$ gives $191 + x \ge 260 \Rightarrow x \ge 69$.

Also $x \le 100$. So $69 \le x \le 100$: the least score is $69$, and the possible scores are $\{69, 70, 71, \ldots, 100\}$.

questions.solution_md: Translate each condition into an inequation, solve it, and then apply the conditions of the situation (whole numbers, odd numbers, a maximum of 100).

marking_scheme.step: (c) least score 69 and the set with x ≤ 100

Answer each part.

(a) Start from $3 < 8$. Write the true statement you get when both sides are (i) multiplied by $2$ (ii) multiplied by $-2$ (iii) divided by $-1$. What rule do (ii) and (iii) illustrate?

(b) Solve $-3x + 7 > 2 - x$, $x \in \mathbb{W}$.

(c) Find the integers that satisfy both $3 - 2x \ge x - 12$ and $4x + 5 > -7$, and describe how they appear on a number line.

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) (i) $6 < 16$ (ii) $-6 > -16$ (iii) $-3 > -8$. Multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number reverses the inequality sign; a positive number keeps it.

(b) $-3x + 7 > 2 - x \Rightarrow -2x > -5 \Rightarrow x < 2.5$. Solution set $= \{0, 1, 2\}$.

So $-3 < x \le 5$ with $x \in \mathbb{Z}$: $\{-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$. On a number line: eight filled dots at $-2$ to $5$, none at $-3$.

The two number lines below show solution sets.

(a) Row (a) shows a solution set for $x \in \mathbb{Z}$. Write it in roster form and in set-builder form.

(b) Row (b) shows a solution set for $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Write it in set-builder form, and write a linear inequation with whole-number coefficients that has this solution set.

(c) Solve $-1 < \dfrac{5 - 3x}{2} \le 4$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$, and describe its graph on the number line.

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Roster: $\{-2, -1, 0, 1\}$. Set-builder: $\{x : x \in \mathbb{Z},\ -2 \le x \le 1\}$ (equivalently $-3 < x < 2$).

(b) $\{x : x \in \mathbb{R},\ x > -1.5\}$. Multiplying $x > -1.5$ by $2$ gives $2x > -3$, so one such inequation is $2x + 3 > 0$.

(c) Multiply by $2$: $-2 < 5 - 3x \le 8$. Subtract $5$: $-7 < -3x \le 3$. Divide by $-3$ and reverse both signs: $\dfrac{7}{3} > x \ge -1$.

Solution set $= \{x : x \in \mathbb{R},\ -1 \le x < \dfrac{7}{3}\}$. Number line: a filled circle at $-1$, an open circle at $\dfrac{7}{3}$ (about $2.33$) and a thick line joining them.

questions.stem_md:
Answer each part.

(a) Solve $2x - 5 \le 5x + 4$ and write the solution set when $x \in \mathbb{N}$, $x \in \mathbb{W}$ and $x \in \mathbb{Z}$.

(b) Describe how the solution sets for $x \in \mathbb{Z}$ and for $x \in \mathbb{R}$ look on a number line, and explain the difference.

(c) Solve the combined inequation $2x - 5 \le 5x + 4 < 3x + 11$ for $x \in \mathbb{Z}$ and state how many integers satisfy it.

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) $2x - 5 \le 5x + 4 \Rightarrow -3x \le 9 \Rightarrow x \ge -3$.

$x \in \mathbb{N}$: $\{1, 2, 3, \ldots\}$; $x \in \mathbb{W}$: $\{0, 1, 2, \ldots\}$; $x \in \mathbb{Z}$: $\{-3, -2, -1, \ldots\}$.

(b) For $\mathbb{Z}$: separate filled dots at $-3, -2, -1, 0, \ldots$, continuing to the right. For $\mathbb{R}$: a filled circle at $-3$ and a thick line with an arrow to the right, because every real number from $-3$ onwards (such as $-2.5$) is included, not just the integers.

(c) Left part from (a): $x \ge -3$. Right part: $5x + 4 < 3x + 11 \Rightarrow 2x < 7 \Rightarrow x < 3.5$.

So $-3 \le x < 3.5$, and the solution set is $\{-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3\}$: $7$ integers.
